anchors.1: Related information is scattered with no discernible grouping; the reader must hunt across the whole page to assemble any one concept.
anchors.3: Basic grouping exists (e.g. issuer vs. customer are visually separate) but placement is inconsistent or some related fields are still split across distant regions.
anchors.4: Every field lives in one clearly bounded group matching the domain's natural structure, each in an expected location.
anchors.5: Grouping is clear AND the zones are ordered to match the reader's natural scanning path, so the reader never backtracks to find related information.

anchors.1: Every field has the same size/weight; no single fact stands out from the rest.
anchors.3: Some size/weight variation exists, but the one fact the reader needs first is not clearly the most prominent element on the page.
anchors.4: The one fact the reader needs first is visually dominant — larger and/or bolder than everything else.
anchors.5: The key fact is dominant AND every other element recedes in proportion to its importance, producing one unambiguous focal point.

anchors.1: The layout could be mistaken for a different kind of document entirely; it lacks the conventional elements a reader expects for this document type.
anchors.3: The document is recognizable as the right family but is missing one or more conventional elements a reader would expect.
anchors.4: The document includes and positions the conventional elements a reader of this domain expects.
anchors.5: The document is indistinguishable in structure and convention from a real-world professional document of this type.

anchors.1: No navigational aids exist — a wall of unlabeled text or numbers with no alignment or whitespace to guide scanning.
anchors.3: Some labels exist, but alignment or whitespace is inconsistent.
anchors.4: Labels, alignment, and whitespace are applied consistently throughout.
anchors.5: Affordances actively anticipate the reader's exact scanning path.

anchors.1: Type sizing/weight is arbitrary or inconsistent; text is cramped, overflowing, or wrapped awkwardly.
anchors.3: Sizing/weight is mostly consistent, but a few awkward line breaks or spacing issues remain.
anchors.4: Sizing, weight, and spacing are consistent throughout with no awkward breaks.
anchors.5: Every typographic choice reads as intentional — a coherent, deliberate type system with zero awkward breaks.

anchors.1: The document is visually noisy or internally inconsistent across sections.
anchors.3: The document is mostly restrained, but one or two decorative inconsistencies remain.
anchors.4: The document is fully restrained and internally consistent.
anchors.5: The document is restrained, consistent, AND every visual element earns its place — nothing could be removed without losing information.

gates.label: Reading order
gates.description: The rendered PDF's content reads top-to-bottom, left-to-right in the same order a human would naturally scan it, with no illogical jumps between regions. Pass/fail, no partial credit.

gates.label: Print safety
gates.description: The document renders correctly at its actual print/paper size: no clipped text or table columns at page margins, and no essential content lost or orphaned across a page break. Pass/fail, no partial credit.

stress_exemption.reason: Stress-matrix fixtures (test/rendro/edge_matrix_test.exs) exist to prove pipeline robustness and byte-determinism under adversarial inputs -- overflow, extreme text length, empty/60+ line-item counts, numeric edge cases, currency and page-size variance -- not reader-facing aesthetic quality. They are deliberately excluded from the reader-quality rubric's beauty gate; the gate applies only to curated family x domain demonstration documents.

justifications.information_architecture: Issuer letterhead, then a bounded Bill To/date/due/terms block, then the line-item table, then subtotal/tax/total — each zone bounded and ordered to match the reader's natural top-to-bottom scan (who's billing -> who's billed/when -> what for -> how much) with no backtracking.
justifications.content_hierarchy: Re-rendered raster measured: 'Total Due: $696.60' glyph height is 24px, vs. 19px for the 'INVOICE #...' title and 10-16px for every other line — Total Due is the single largest element on the page and the unambiguous focal point.
justifications.domain_fit: Issuer address, invoice number, bill-to, due date, payment terms (Net 30), itemized qty/price table, and subtotal/tax/total breakdown together read as a real small-business invoice, not a toy layout.
justifications.reader_affordances: Item/Qty/Price column headers, consistent column alignment, and a clearly labeled subtotal/tax/total stack make the math easy to trace.
justifications.typographic_craft: Consistent 2-decimal money throughout (the prior $79.0 defect is gone); one item description wraps to a second line but wraps cleanly at a word boundary with no overlap or orphan.
justifications.restraint_cohesion: Restrained and internally consistent; no decorative noise. The lower two-thirds of the page is blank because the fixture has only 5 line items — empty space, not visual clutter.

justifications.information_architecture: Account header, statement period, and opening balance are grouped, immediately followed by the boxed closing-balance summary, then the transaction ledger — matching the way a statement reader actually scans (bottom line first, then verify against detail).
justifications.content_hierarchy: Re-rendered raster measured: the boxed 'Closing balance $6,647.56' glyph height is 26px, vs. 19px for the account title and 16px for every transaction row — the closing balance is now the single largest, unambiguous focal point (previously a small Balance-column cell).
justifications.domain_fit: Masked account number, statement period, opening balance, boxed closing balance, and a running-balance ledger with parenthesized debits read as a conventional bank/ledger statement.
justifications.reader_affordances: Clear Date/Description/Amount/Balance columns with a running balance make it easy to trace any line.
justifications.typographic_craft: Consistent money formatting and clean alignment throughout, including the new closing-balance box.

justifications.information_architecture: The merchant identity (Harbor & Oak Cafe + address) now heads the render, followed by the sales-receipt/guest/date block, item table, and totals — each group bounded and ordered top-to-bottom the way a receipt is naturally scanned.
justifications.content_hierarchy: Re-rendered raster measured: 'Total: $30.78' glyph height is 22px, vs. 17-19px for the merchant name/address and 10-13px for item rows — Total is now the single largest element and the clear focal point (previously small text at the bottom).
justifications.domain_fit: Merchant name/address, Sales Receipt label, item list, and subtotal/tax/total now read as a conventional retail receipt (previously missing the merchant identity entirely).
justifications.reader_affordances: Description/Amount columns plus a subtotal/tax/total breakdown make the math easy to follow.
justifications.typographic_craft: Clean and consistent money and alignment.

justifications.information_architecture: Content is now vertically and horizontally centered within the border as a single ceremonial flow (title -> 'this certifies that' -> recipient -> body -> date -> signatory), matching the order a reader naturally scans a certificate.
justifications.content_hierarchy: Re-rendered raster measured: 'Alex Rivera' glyph height is 34px, vs. 26px for the 'Certificate of Completion' title and 11-15px for the body/date/signature lines — the recipient name is now the single largest element and unambiguous focal point (previously the title dominated).
justifications.domain_fit: Centered, bordered, ceremonial layout with title/recipient/body/date/signatory reads as a real-world certificate, not a top-left log entry.
justifications.reader_affordances: Centering and the width-constrained (68%) body paragraph guide the eye down the page consistently; no explicit field labels are needed for this document type.
justifications.typographic_craft: Consistent sizing/weight; the body paragraph now wraps within its constrained width with clean line breaks instead of running edge-to-edge.
justifications.restraint_cohesion: Vertical centering replaces the prior top-packed layout; restrained and internally consistent.

justifications.information_architecture: Employer/employee header, the Net Pay box, and the earnings/deductions table (now separated by a spacer column) are each clearly bounded and ordered net-pay-first, matching how a payslip is scanned.
justifications.content_hierarchy: Net Pay $3,292.50 in a large boxed line remains unambiguously dominant over the table and header text.
justifications.domain_fit: Reads as a conventional UK payslip: PAYE, National Insurance, pension, tax code, YTD columns.
justifications.reader_affordances: Re-rendered raster confirmed the header row now reads 'YTD Deductions' with a clear space (a narrow spacer column separates the groups) instead of the prior 'YTDDeductions' collision.
justifications.typographic_craft: Data cells now render at a consistent explicit size 11 and the widened YTD columns (60pt) let '$25,200.00' fit on one line without wrapping a digit.

justifications.information_architecture: Event header, the SECTION/ROW/SEAT/GATE locator group, and the perforated reference stub are each clearly grouped and ordered top-to-bottom the way a ticket is scanned at the door.
justifications.content_hierarchy: Re-rendered on native A6: measured glyph height of the 'GA H 24 B' locator line is 27px, vs. ~14px per line for the event title and ~10-11px for the terms footer — the seat-assignment readout is now the single largest element on the page and the unambiguous focal point.
justifications.domain_fit: Perforated stub, reference number, non-transferable terms, and a section/row/seat/gate locator read as a real ticket.
justifications.reader_affordances: SECTION/ROW/SEAT/GATE labels sit directly above their large values, and the perforation affordance makes the tear-off stub obvious.
justifications.typographic_craft: Clean, consistent type; the wrapped event title and terms footer both wrap cleanly at word boundaries on the narrower A6 width.
justifications.restraint_cohesion: Native A6 sizing (297.64 x 419.53pt) replaces the prior A6-content-on-A4-canvas mismatch; the page is well-proportioned to its content with no decorative noise, though the terms footer leaves some blank space beneath it.
